decisions.executionNote: Begin raised approach to the upright blue bottle with left arm, keeping right parked; small initial increments preserve elbow configuration.
Align left above blue bottle for a side grasp, and start right approach toward yellow bottle in its own workspace.
Seat blue bottle between left fingers and close; right continues open approach to yellow. Retention will be checked visually on lift.
Lift the blue bottle and start leftward bin transit; finish seating yellow in right fingers and close, with both hands remaining on their own sides.
Blue did not travel with left gripper; reopen and approach its body lower. Lift yellow with right and check retention before preparing a handover.
Yellow is retained; bring it toward a central handover with right wrist turning inward. Clear the now-lying blue bottle and orient left to receive without crossing arms.
Present yellow near the centerline with right facing left; advance left facing right below the donor grasp, keeping both EE positions on their own sides.
Insert left fingers around the yellow bottle below the right grasp and close the receiver while donor remains closed.
Test handover: keep left closed, open right and withdraw donor slowly. Bottle tilted during closure, so confirm receiver retention visually.
Yellow slipped onto the central tabletop during handover. Reopen and lower left for recovery; withdraw right to its own side while returning its yaw.
Yellow has rolled clear to the right. Switch left to a top-down recovery of the blue lying bottle, lifting and rotating with clearance; park right.
Replan from unchanged pose after continuity rejection: halve translation and wrist rotation while lifting away from the table.
Continue open left overhead approach to the blue bottle; gradually turn the gripper downward, with right stationary clear of the path.
Finish turning left fingers downward over the lying blue bottle, maintaining an elevated wrist and open gripper for visual alignment.
After the wrist-rotation continuity stop, retain current near-downward orientation and shift back-left onto the blue bottle body with a shallow descent.
Use wrist view to center farther left and lower around the blue bottle body, then close without moving the wrist.
Lift the closed left grasp slowly to verify blue-bottle retention, then begin moving toward the left bin.
Blue was not retained. Reopen and correct toward its middle rather than its end, lowering the near-vertical left gripper for a new grasp.
Fine-center on the blue bottle's cylindrical body and lower two centimeters, then close left while stationary to avoid pushing it along the table.
Lift the centered blue grasp and start a cautious leftward transfer; keep fingers fully closed and confirm the bottle moves with them.
Blue is visibly traveling in the closed left grasp. Carry it left toward the bin while gently easing the wrist out of the downward orientation.
No motion executed after continuity rejection. Retry the held-bottle transit at half translation and wrist increments, staying on the existing elbow-up branch.
Continue carrying the visibly held blue bottle over the left-side bin, keeping its height and closing target fixed.
Place the blue bottle well within the bin footprint and open left fingers to drop it; hold the wrist still during release.
Leave left open after the blue drop and move above the front white bottle, rotating the closing direction perpendicular to its horizontal axis.
Advance left above the horizontal white bottle, continuing the downward-grasp orientation and a controlled descent.
Keep the near-downward wrist orientation fixed and lower left around the white bottle body, with a small rightward alignment correction before closing.
Close left around the white bottle, pause for seating, then make a short vertical test lift to check retention.
Continue lifting the white bottle with left closed and begin the binward transit, checking that it follows rather than remaining on the table.
White bottle is moving with left fingers. Carry it above the left bin with a small upward clearance and no wrist reorientation.
Move the white bottle farther inside the bin rim, then release with left open and hold position to observe the drop.
Two bottles are visible in the bin. Move left above the green bottle while adjusting jaw direction; prepare an overhead right grasp of the fallen yellow bottle.
Bring left over the green body and right over yellow, keeping a clear separation and turning right progressively downward before grasp descent.
Replan from the executed two-step prefix. Halve right-arm increments to preserve wrist continuity while left continues its separated overhead approach.
Use wrist views to center left on the green body with a shallow descent. Continue right's gradual downward rotation above yellow, keeping both grippers open.
Correct green's small lateral offset before closing left; center and seat the yellow body in right fingers, then close without further wrist motion.
Test-lift both closed grasps; shift green slightly left to clear the center while yellow rises vertically. Judge retention from the next views.
Green follows left, so carry it binward. Yellow stayed on the table; reopen right and reseat slightly lower with a small lateral correction.
Continue green toward the left bin. Recenter the yellow body between right fingers from the wrist view, seat six millimeters lower, and close while stationary.
Carry green fully over the bin; test-lift the reseated right yellow grasp while keeping both fingers closed.
Release green over the bin without further left motion after the wrist-wrap guard. Yellow again slipped; make right's approach more vertical and reseat the open fingers lower.

Green has dropped into the bin. Withdraw left and unwind its wrist. Right wrist view shows yellow left of the jaw center; shift toward it before another stationary closure, without forcing the descent.
Test-lift the newly centered yellow grasp. Bring left to a clear receiving position, keeping the two arms separated.
Yellow did not follow the lift. Reopen right and descend farther around its body, correcting the wrist-view lateral offset while left waits clear.
Close the right fingers around the now-centered yellow body at the lower seating height, then make a short vertical retention test.
Yellow is now visibly retained. Raise it toward the centerline with right closed; turn left toward a horizontal receiving grasp at the bottle's free end.
Turn the donor bottle so its long free end will face left for a separated handover. Lower and level the open receiver outside the turning bottle's path.
Replan with smaller receiver rotation after the continuity guard. Level left at bottle height while presenting the donor's free bottle end toward the left.
Keep donor steady and approach its free bottle end with left. Reduce receiver rotation to eight milliradians per step after the wrist continuity stop.
Advance the open receiver slowly around the yellow bottle's free base while the donor remains fixed and closed; retain vertical separation between wrists.
Insert receiver another centimeter around the free bottle base and close left while right keeps holding; check the shared grasp before releasing donor.
Release the donor and withdraw it upward while left maintains the base grasp, then make a short receiver lift to verify the handover.
Yellow is hanging from the left receiver after release. Carry it leftward and turn toward the bin, while withdrawing and gradually leveling the empty right arm.
Continue the retained yellow bottle toward the bin with left closed; bring the empty right arm back toward its home side with smooth wrist leveling.
Carry the final retained bottle farther inside the left bin footprint before release; continue the empty right arm's smooth return.
Open left over the bin to release yellow and hold through the drop. Move the empty right arm closer to its origin with smooth leveling.
